answer: A market for nebula photos, sonnet recordings and sparrow calls can charge admission in verified upload bandwidth. At each unpredictable epoch beacon, every earning key has 30 seconds to stream 64 MiB of pseudorandom bytes derived from that beacon and its key. The verifier counts actual bytes received and rejects compressed or mismatched streams. One stream cannot qualify another key. Keeping k aliases eligible costs 64 times k MiB of outbound traffic in the same window; sharing one connection divides its capacity instead of duplicating it.
